after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $⌈x⌉$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x:$ 

$$
⌈x⌉=n,\,\text{where}\,n-1<x\le n,\,n\in Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=0.4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.4) & =⌈\sqrt{\frac{0.4}{2.5}}⌉ \\  & =⌈\sqrt{0.16}⌉ \\  & =⌈0.4⌉.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$
⌈0.4⌉=1.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.4) & =⌈0.4⌉ \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $⌈x⌉$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x:$ 

$$
⌈x⌉=n,\,\text{where}\,n-1<x\le n,\,n\in Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=0.2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.2) & =(⌈1-2(0.2)⌉+1)^{2} \\  & =(⌈1-0.4⌉+1)^{2} \\  & =(⌈0.6⌉+1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$
⌈0.6⌉=1.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.2) & =(⌈0.6⌉+1)^{2} \\  & =(1+1)^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: 8/1.5 = 16/3 = 5⅓, whose floor is 5. Therefore f(1.5) = e^5.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $⌊x⌋$ equals the greatest integer that is less than or equal to $x:$

$$
⌊x⌋=n,\,\text{where}\,n\le x<n+1,\,n\in Z.
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=1.5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.5) & ={e}^{⌊8/1.5⌋} \\  & ={e}^{⌊5.333…⌋}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have

$$
⌊5.333…⌋=5.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.5) & ={e}^{⌊5.333…⌋} \\  & ={e}^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the value of f(x)=e⌊8/x⌋ at x=1.5.

a
e8
b
e5
c
e4
d
e7
e
e6
Submit

EXPLANATION

Suppose x is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function ⌊x⌋ equals the greatest integer that is less than or equal to x: ⌊x⌋=n,wheren≤x<n+1,n∈Z.

Evaluating f(x) at x=1.5, we get f(1.5)=e⌊8/1.5⌋=e⌊5.333…⌋.

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have ⌊5.333…⌋=5.

Therefore, we conclude that f(1.5)=e⌊5.333…⌋=e5.

content.worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $⌊x⌋$ equals the greatest integer that is less than or equal to $x:$

$$
⌊x⌋=n,\,\text{where}\,n\le x<n+1,\,n\in Z.
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=1.5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.5) & ={e}^{⌊8/1.5⌋} \\  & ={e}^{⌊5.333…⌋}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have

$$
⌊5.333…⌋=5.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.5) & ={e}^{⌊5.333…⌋} \\  & ={e}^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find the value of $f(x)=x{e}^{⌈x+0.6⌉}$ at $x=1.2.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $⌈x⌉$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x:$ 

$$
⌈x⌉=n,\,\text{where}\,n-1<x\le n,\,n\in Z
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=1.2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.2) & =1.2{e}^{⌈1.2+0.6⌉} \\  & =1.2{e}^{⌈1.8⌉}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$
⌈1.8⌉=2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.2) & =1.2{e}^{⌈1.8⌉} \\  & =1.2{e}^{2} \\  & =1.2(7.389\,05…) \\  & =8.866\,86… \\  & ≈8.87,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
